clue.text: Rationalists appeal on behalf of Russian intellectuals

definitions.meaning: people who reject dogma and reason their own way to belief

definitions.text: appeal on behalf of Russian intellectuals
definitions.meaning: a campaign slogan demanding release for imprisoned dissident thinkers, read as an imperative phrase

explanation.surface: Sceptical campaigners make a plea for the liberty of dissidents jailed in the Soviet Union.
explanation.definitionFit: Rationalists and the second reading's call to liberate jailed scholars share one two-word phrase meaning people who form opinions independently of authority.

clue.text: Sole comfort for a highwayman

definitions.meaning: a cushion placed under the bottom of the foot
a robber who preyed on travellers

explanation.surface: Wondering what a highwayman's only consolation might be.
explanation.definitionFit: A cushion for the underside of the foot and an old word for a robber who held up travellers on foot share this spelling.

clue.text: Do head off

definitions.meaning: to carry out or perform a task
to behead, cut someone's head off

explanation.surface: A terse instruction to set off or perform some action.
explanation.definitionFit: One verb means both to carry out a plan and to put a condemned person to death, as by beheading.

clue.text: First leaf of any book, or any leaf of Debrett

definitions.meaning: the opening sheet bearing the book's name and author
every sheet of Debrett's, a British guide to the peerage, lists lords and ladies

explanation.surface: Comparing the opening sheet of an ordinary book with the contents of a peerage directory.
explanation.walkthrough: Debrett's Peerage is a British reference book listing aristocrats, so every sheet of it is filled with nobles' ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: The opening sheet of a book names it, while every sheet of a peerage guide is a list of aristocratic ranks: both are sheets of names or ranks.

clue.text: Country which takes in reciprocal aid

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: reciprocal suggests something turned back the other way, so the word for help is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A nation that accepts aid given in return for favours.
explanation.definitionFit: A large South Asian nation, the world's most populous republic.

clue.text: Joint near which indecent re marks are made

definitions.text: Joint near which indecent re marks are made

parts.words: Joint near which indecent re marks are made
parts.note: a finger joint, recalling the idiom for risque comments that come close to it, being near the bone of decency

explanation.surface: Bawdy comments are made close to some part of the body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Near the' followed by this finger joint is an idiom for jokes that are almost indecent.
explanation.definitionFit: A finger joint, and the idiom about near-indecent humour names exactly this body part.

clue.text: Tear net woven into rough dress fabric

indicators.note: weaving threads together rearranges them, signalling the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Ripped netting is incorporated into a coarse garment material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woven' rearranges TEAR NET; 'into' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A coarse woollen cloth used historically for clothing.

clue.text: All males are knaves, without exception

parts.note: all males means every man
a knave in a card pack is the jack

explanation.surface: A cynic's sweeping claim that all men are rogues.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'knaves' are rogues, but in cards the knave is the jack.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means every single person, everybody with no one left out.

clue.text: Neutral in colour, but not in temperament!

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the colour word

parts.note: violet is a colour
N is the abbreviation for neutral, as on electrical plugs

explanation.surface: Someone calm in their colouring but anything but calm in character.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads 'not neutral in temperament': the result, an unrestrained temper, is the opposite of neutral.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not at all neutral in disposition is furious and aggressive.

clue.text: Theologian heartened by note to relative is put off

indicators.note: heartened is read as given a heart, so the theologian's letters have something placed in the middle

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree

indicators.note: to means the note is attached after the relative

parts.note: an aunt is a relative
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A divinity scholar, cheered by a letter to a family member, is discouraged.
explanation.definitionFit: Discouraged or intimidated, deterred from acting.

clue.text: If dentist can mix it, he could use it in a mouthwash

definitions.text: he could use it in a mouthwash

indicators.note: mixing rearranges, so the letters of the first three words are shuffled

explanation.surface: A dentist preparing a germ-killing rinse for the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A germicide, the antiseptic agent a dental practitioner might add to a rinse.

clue.text: Somehow put into rare state of excitement

indicators.note: into places the shuffled letters inside the word rare

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters arrive in some unspecified order

explanation.surface: Somehow pushed into an unusual state of thrill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' looks like a vague adverb in the surface but signals the shuffle; 'into' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstasy, an intense feeling of joy or delight.

clue.text: They go around decoratively on foot

definitions.text: They go around decoratively on foot

parts.words: They go around decoratively on foot
parts.note: describes ornamental bands worn encircling the lower leg, not pedestrians strolling for show

explanation.surface: People promenading for show rather than travelling by car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go around' suggests walking about; here it means encircling the leg just above the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornamental chains or bands worn round the lowest part of the leg.

clue.text: Little irritating it is

parts.note: a tiny biting gnat, small and annoying

explanation.surface: A remark that something is a minor nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny biting insect, notoriously small and annoying, a summer pest.

clue.text: He attacked the city of Paris-a brave Frenchman, non?

definitions.text: He attacked the city of Paris

parts.note: brave means game, as in game for anything
M is short for Monsieur, a Frenchman
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking whether a courageous Frenchman assaulted the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Paris here is the Trojan prince, not the French capital: his city was Troy, besieged by the Greek leader.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek king led the siege of Troy, the city of the Trojan prince who abducted Helen.

clue.text: A sober conclusion turning up

parts.note: TT is teetotal, abstaining from alcohol
an ending is a conclusion

explanation.surface: A sober ending emerging.
explanation.definitionFit: Being present at an event, the same as showing up there.

clue.text: Daily supplier not used to a man from Cape Town

parts.note: something not used is new
SA for South Africa, home of Cape Town, plus GENT for a man

explanation.surface: A paper deliverer who is new to a South African.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'daily' is a daily newspaper, so its supplier is a shop selling papers.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopkeeper who sells the daily papers.

clue.text: He designed planes to shape wood

definitions.meaning: Frank ..., the British engineer who invented the jet engine
to carve wood with a knife

explanation.surface: An aircraft designer who also smooths timber with carpentry planes.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank Whittle was the English engineer who pioneered jet propulsion; 'planes' tempts as the carpenter's tool.
explanation.definitionFit: The engineer pioneered jet aircraft engines, and the verb means to carve timber by paring off shavings.

clue.text: Name bit thrown all around

indicators.note: thrown suggests letters tossed about and landing in a new order

explanation.surface: A label with a piece tossed about everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambient describes the surrounding environment, what is present on every side.

clue.text: Sounds a promising path for a promising couple

indicators.note: sounds signals the word is identified by how it is pronounced

parts.note: I'll, short for I will, is a promise

explanation.surface: A hopeful route for a hopeful pair.
explanation.walkthrough: A couple making vows walk this church passage; 'promising' plays on making promises in marriage, and 'I'll' is the promise heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedding couple walk down the church's central passage on the way to exchanging vows.

clue.text: Stupid fellow for example needs best possible weapon

parts.note: an ass is a fool
eg abbreviates exempli gratia, for example
A1 means first-rate, here written AI

explanation.surface: A fool, for instance, requires the finest arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A slender spear used by southern African peoples.

clue.text: A feminist explosion is a common American affair

parts.note: a feminine person is a she
a bang is an explosion

explanation.surface: A women's-rights outburst is typical in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the whole shebang' is an American idiom meaning the entire business.
explanation.definitionFit: American slang for a whole matter or business, as in the whole works.

clue.text: Friendly-but not entirely self confident?

definitions.meaning: split as a question, ...?, the doubt of someone unsure of themselves

explanation.surface: Being pleasant but lacking assurance.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word as three words asking whether one is capable.
explanation.definitionFit: Good-natured and agreeable; split into three words it becomes a doubtful question about one's own capability.

clue.text: Where Westphalians go to eat in Germany

definitions.meaning: a city in North Rhine-Westphalia, in the Ruhr
the German verb meaning to eat

explanation.surface: German locals heading out for a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ruhr city lies in North Rhine-Westphalia, and the same word is the German infinitive for dining.

clue.text: Just beginning the north face of the Eiger

parts.note: a climb up the Eiger's face is an ascent

explanation.surface: Just starting out on the famous north wall of a Swiss mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: The Eiger is a Swiss Alpine peak whose north face is a famous climb.
explanation.definitionFit: Emerging or newly forming, at the earliest stage.

clue.text: What people have if nervous-of mice

definitions.text: What people have if nervous-of mice

parts.words: What people have if nervous-of mice
parts.note: the idiom for being in a state of panic is to have young cats; and young cats are what rodents dread

explanation.surface: Asking what people suffer when afraid of rodents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having' these is British slang for being very anxious, and they also happen to be what mice fear.
explanation.definitionFit: Young cats, the idiom for panicking, and also predators that rodents rightly fear.

clue.text: Instil knowledge of where flour is produced

definitions.meaning: to fix firmly in the mind
split as two words, inside cereal seeds, from which flour is milled

explanation.surface: Teaching someone about the place where flour comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knowledge of' is a link; the second reading splits the word into two.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to fix deeply in the mind, and split it locates flour within cereal kernels.

clue.text: Starting by obtaining assessment of course

parts.note: obtaining is getting
the going is the official report on the state of a racecourse's turf

explanation.surface: Beginning by acquiring an evaluation of a programme of study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' suggests study but means a racecourse; the going is its ground condition, as soft or firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Setting off or commencing, the same as making a start.
